supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Let $(M,g,N,o)$ be an oriented, time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, with metric-selected Levi-Civita connection $\nabla$. Let $\mathcal U\subseteq M$ be open, let $u,V,s\in C^\infty(\mathcal U,\mathbb R)$, and let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $\mathcal U$. Define
$$\Box_g u:=\nabla^a\nabla_a u,\qquad |du|_g^2:=g^{ab}(\nabla_a u)(\nabla_b u).$$
If $\Box_g u=Vu+s$, define the symmetric covariant tensor
$$T_{ab}[u,V]:=(\nabla_a u)(\nabla_b u)-\frac12g_{ab}\bigl(|du|_g^2+Vu^2\bigr),$$
the vector current $J_X^a:=g^{ac}T_{cb}X^b$, and the scalar deformation term $K_X:=T_{ab}\nabla^{(a}X^{b)}$, where $\nabla^{(a}X^{b)}=(\nabla^aX^b+\nabla^bX^a)/2$.

For a finite smooth singular $3$-chain $\Sigma=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i\sigma_i$ with $k\ge0$ and $c_i\in\mathbb R$, take each simplex $\sigma_i$ to be a map $\Delta^3\to\mathcal U$ that extends smoothly to a map into $M$ on an open neighborhood of $\Delta^3$ in its affine span. Here
$$\Delta^3:=\{(t_0,t_1,t_2,t_3)\in\mathbb R^4:t_j\ge0,\ \sum_{j=0}^3t_j=1\},$$
with its standard orientation from the ordered vertices $e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3$, where each $e_j$ is the $j$th standard basis vector of $\mathbb R^4$. Define the local flux by
$$\Phi_{J_X}(\Sigma):=\sum_{i=1}^k c_i\int_{\Delta^3}\sigma_i^*(\iota_{J_X}\mathrm{vol}_g).$$

Here $\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the oriented metric $4$-form whose expression in an oriented chart is $\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}\,dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and $\iota_{J_X}\mathrm{vol}_g$ is the $3$-form that sends $(Y_1,Y_2,Y_3)\in(T_pM)^3$ to $\mathrm{vol}_{g,p}(J_X(p),Y_1,Y_2,Y_3)$ at each $p\in\mathcal U$. The map $\sigma_i^*$ is pullback of differential forms, and each simplex integral uses the pullback form-integration convention of the metric-volume current-flux definition listed in the following references section. Linearity makes the sum independent of the written chain representation. The integral uses the differential-form convention on null faces and assigns no flux to a chain with points outside $\mathcal U$; it never extends $J_X$ outside $\mathcal U$. In length coordinates, if $u$ has unit $[u]$, then $V$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-2}$, $s$ has unit $[u]\mathrm m^{-2}$, and the components of $T$ have unit $[u]^2\mathrm m^{-2}$; no physical normalization of $u$ or $X$ is imposed.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $M,q_e,q_m\in\mathbb R$ be length parameters. Set
$Q^2:=q_e^2+q_m^2$ and
$$f(r):=1-\frac{2M}{r}+\frac{Q^2}{r^2}.$$
The selected ingoing RN manifold is
$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}:=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2,$$
where $v,r$ have units of metres, $S^2$ has unit round metric $\gamma$ and
outward area form $\omega$, and the signature is $(-,+,+,+)$. Orient the
product by $dv\wedge dr\wedge\omega$. Define
$$g_{\mathrm{in}}=-f(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma,\qquad \mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}=-\frac{q_e}{r^2}\,dv\wedge dr+q_m\omega.$$
These are smooth on every $r>0$, including every positive root of $f$; the
domain excludes $r=0$. This is an extension of the static RN metric and field,
not a maximal extension or a specification of a source at the excluded
centre.

For the time orientation, define the global smooth fields
$$\ell:=-\partial_r,\qquad n:=\partial_v+\frac{f(r)}2\partial_r,\qquad N:=\ell+n=\partial_v+\left(\frac{f(r)}2-1\right)\partial_r.$$
The chosen future timelike field is $N$; the future cone is the component of
the timelike cone containing it. The well-definedness proof shows that $N$ is
timelike and that $\ell,n$ are future null. On $f\ne0$, the substitution
$v=t+r_*(r)$ with $r_*'=1/f$ identifies the metric and two-form with the
static dyonic RN formulas of [[def-emg-xs-rn-data]]. This coordinate
identification does not assert agreement of time orientations on the
interior static components: on $f>0$ the selected orientation agrees with
$\partial_t$, while on $f<0$ it is the opposite of the separate choice
$\partial_r$ made by that static definition.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $M>0$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2>0$, and use
$f(r)=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2$ on the selected ingoing RN model. If $M^2\ge Q^2$,
the positive roots
$$r_\pm=M\pm\sqrt{M^2-Q^2}$$
are null constant-$r$ hypersurfaces. For the Killing field $\xi=\partial_v$
normalized by the displayed coordinate for which
$g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ as $r\to\infty$, each is a Killing horizon in the
local sense of
[[def-emg-causal-solution-and-horizon-vocabulary]], with signed surface
gravity
$$\kappa_\pm=\frac{f'(r_\pm)}2 =\frac{r_\pm-r_\mp}{2r_\pm^2}.$$
At extremality $M^2=Q^2$, the coincident root is $r_H=M$ and
$\kappa_H=0$. If $M^2<Q^2$, $f$ has no positive root and no constant-$r$
null hypersurface of this form. These are local properties of the selected
metric; they do not classify event horizons in a maximal spacetime.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Fix real parameters $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m$ with $q_e^2+q_m^2=m^2$, and use the selected ingoing dyonic Reissner–Nordström metric on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$:

$$g=-D(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad D(r)=\left(1-\frac mr\right)^2.$$

Here $\gamma_{S^2}$ is the metric induced on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ by the Euclidean metric, and $\omega_{S^2}$ is its outward area form. The coordinates $v,r$ and parameters $m,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres; angular coordinates are dimensionless. The displayed Maxwell two-form uses the supplied geometric normalization, with no additional SI normalization: its $vr$ coordinate component has units $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and its angular components have units $\mathrm m$. In the supplied ingoing RN background with mass parameter $M=m$, the fixed Maxwell two-form is

$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}=-q_e r^{-2}\,dv\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$

Use the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection; in every smooth chart its coefficients are $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})$ and are smooth. For the horizon-data result, set $M=m$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2=M^2$ and $f(r):=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2=D(r)$. It states that $\xi=\partial_v$ obeys $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ and is normalized by $g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ as $r\to\infty$; at $r=M$, $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=f(M)=0$, $\xi^\flat=dr$, and $\xi$ is tangent to the level. Thus $r=m$ is the local Killing horizon generated by $\xi$, with signed surface gravity fixed by $d(g(\xi,\xi))=-2\kappa_H\xi^\flat$ and equal to $\kappa_H=f'(M)/2=0$ (units $\mathrm m^{-1}$). No maximal-extension or global event-horizon assertion is included. The metric and displayed Maxwell field are fixed. A neutral test scalar has no electromagnetic gauge coupling or scalar coupling to that field, and does not source either background.

A reduced spherical scalar profile is a real function $\psi:\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\to\mathbb R$ whose coordinate partial derivatives through total order three are continuous. Its full scalar on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the spherical lift $\widetilde\psi(v,r,\omega):=\psi(v,r)$; in radial formulas we use $\psi(v,r)$ for the reduced profile, and the notation $\Box_g\psi=0$ means $\Box_g\widetilde\psi=0$. For a $C^3$ scalar lift, define the extension of the smooth-scalar wave operator by the trace of its $C^1$ scalar Hessian,

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi:=g^{ab}\bigl(\partial_a\partial_b\widetilde\psi-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\partial_c\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

The second-order chain rule and the connection-coefficient transformation law make these components a covariant $2$-tensor, so the trace is chart independent and $C^1$. This agrees with the supplied smooth-scalar definition when the lift is smooth. In every smooth chart, with $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, metric compatibility and the density formula give

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1w\partial_a\bigl(wg^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

For the spherical lift in an angular chart, $w=r^2\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{AB})}$ and this becomes

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1{r^2}\left[\partial_v(r^2\partial_r\psi)+\partial_r\!\left(r^2(\partial_v\psi+D\partial_r\psi)\right)\right].$$

The density identity used here is stated for smooth vector fields, but its coordinate proof uses only first derivatives of their components and the product rule; it therefore holds for $C^1$ vector fields as well. Here $g^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi$ is $C^2$, so the formula is defined and $\Box_g\widetilde\psi$ is $C^1$. In particular the wave equation can be differentiated once in $r$ for a $C^3$ profile. Set $\phi(v,r)=r\psi(v,r)$ and take every $\partial_r$ derivative in this regular ingoing chart. If $[\psi]$ denotes the arbitrary scalar-field unit, then $[\phi]=[\psi]\,\mathrm m$.

with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

$$f'(x) = 0 \qquad \text{at every interior point } x \text{ of } I .$$

$x \in I$.

differentiable at every interior point of $I$, with $f'(x) = g'(x)$ at every
interior point $x$, then there is a real $k$ with

not a hypothesis of it.

statement.

> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

$$\begin{pmatrix}-D&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
The first block has determinant $-1$, so the full metric density is $w=r^2\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{AB})}$. Put $J^a:=g^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi$. The spherical lift gives $J^v=\psi_r$, $J^r=\psi_v+D\psi_r$, and $J^A=0$; this vector field is $C^2$, so [F2] applies. By [F1], [F3] and metric compatibility, $\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\nabla_aJ^a$. Applying the density formula and cancelling the angular density, which is independent of $v,r$, gives
$$0=\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1{r^2}\left[\partial_v(r^2\psi_r)+\partial_r\!\left(r^2(\psi_v+D\psi_r)\right)\right].$$
Expanding the derivatives and using equality of the continuous mixed partials yields
$$2r^2\psi_{vr}+2r\psi_v+\partial_r(r^2D\psi_r)=0.$$

$$2\phi_{vr}+D\phi_{rr}+D'\phi_r-\frac{D'}r\phi=0.$$

$$g=-D(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad D(r)=\left(1-\frac mr\right)^2.$$

Here $\gamma_{S^2}$ is the metric induced on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ by the Euclidean metric, and $\omega_{S^2}$ is its outward area form. $$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}=-q_e r^{-2}\,dv\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$

For the horizon-data result, set $M=m$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2=M^2$ and $f(r):=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2=D(r)$. It states that $\xi=\partial_v$ obeys $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ and is normalized by $g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ as $r\to\infty$; at $r=M$, $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=f(M)=0$, $\xi^\flat=dr$, and $\xi$ is tangent to the level. Thus $r=m$ is the local Killing horizon generated by $\xi$, with signed surface gravity fixed by $d(g(\xi,\xi))=-2\kappa_H\xi^\flat$ and equal to $\kappa_H=f'(M)/2=0$ (units $\mathrm m^{-1}$). No maximal-extension or global event-horizon assertion is included. The metric and displayed Maxwell field are fixed. A neutral test scalar has no electromagnetic gauge coupling or scalar coupling to that field, and does not source either background.

A reduced spherical scalar profile is a real function $\psi:\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\to\mathbb R$ whose coordinate partial derivatives through total order three are continuous. Its full scalar on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the spherical lift $\widetilde\psi(v,r,\omega):=\psi(v,r)$; in radial formulas we use $\psi(v,r)$ for the reduced profile, and the notation $\Box_g\psi=0$ means $\Box_g\widetilde\psi=0$. For a $C^3$ scalar lift, define the extension of the smooth-scalar wave operator by the trace of its $C^1$ scalar Hessian,

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi:=g^{ab}\bigl(\partial_a\partial_b\widetilde\psi-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\partial_c\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at

([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.

entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map

([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product

$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with

$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Fix real parameters $m>0$ and $q_e,q_m$ with $q_e^2+q_m^2=m^2$, and use the selected ingoing dyonic Reissner–Nordström metric on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}=\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\times S^2$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$:

$$g=-D(r)\,dv^2+2\,dv\,dr+r^2\gamma_{S^2},\qquad D(r)=\left(1-\frac mr\right)^2.$$

Here $\gamma_{S^2}$ is the metric induced on the unit sphere $S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$ by the Euclidean metric, and $\omega_{S^2}$ is its outward area form. The coordinates $v,r$ and parameters $m,q_e,q_m$ have units of metres; angular coordinates are dimensionless. The displayed Maxwell two-form uses the supplied geometric normalization, with no additional SI normalization: its $vr$ coordinate component has units $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and its angular components have units $\mathrm m$. In the supplied ingoing RN background with mass parameter $M=m$, the fixed Maxwell two-form is

$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{in}}=-q_e r^{-2}\,dv\wedge dr+q_m\omega_{S^2}.$$

Use the unique torsion-free, $g$-compatible connection; in every smooth chart its coefficients are $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12g^{ad}(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc})$ and are smooth. For the horizon-data result, set $M=m$, $Q^2=q_e^2+q_m^2=M^2$ and $f(r):=1-2M/r+Q^2/r^2=D(r)$. It states that $\xi=\partial_v$ obeys $\mathcal L_\xi g=0$ and is normalized by $g(\xi,\xi)\to-1$ as $r\to\infty$; at $r=M$, $g^{-1}(dr,dr)=f(M)=0$, $\xi^\flat=dr$, and $\xi$ is tangent to the level. Thus $r=m$ is the local Killing horizon generated by $\xi$, with signed surface gravity fixed by $d(g(\xi,\xi))=-2\kappa_H\xi^\flat$ and equal to $\kappa_H=f'(M)/2=0$ (units $\mathrm m^{-1}$). No maximal-extension or global event-horizon assertion is included. The metric and displayed Maxwell field are fixed. A neutral test scalar has no electromagnetic gauge coupling or scalar coupling to that field, and does not source either background.

A reduced spherical scalar profile is a real function $\psi:\mathbb R_v\times(0,\infty)_r\to\mathbb R$ whose coordinate partial derivatives through total order three are continuous. Its full scalar on $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the spherical lift $\widetilde\psi(v,r,\omega):=\psi(v,r)$; in radial formulas we use $\psi(v,r)$ for the reduced profile, and the notation $\Box_g\psi=0$ means $\Box_g\widetilde\psi=0$. For a $C^3$ scalar lift, define the extension of the smooth-scalar wave operator by the trace of its $C^1$ scalar Hessian,

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi:=g^{ab}\bigl(\partial_a\partial_b\widetilde\psi-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\partial_c\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

The second-order chain rule and the connection-coefficient transformation law make these components a covariant $2$-tensor, so the trace is chart independent and $C^1$. This agrees with the supplied smooth-scalar definition when the lift is smooth. In every smooth chart, with $w=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$, metric compatibility and the density formula give

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1w\partial_a\bigl(wg^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

For the spherical lift in an angular chart, $w=r^2\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{AB})}$ and this becomes

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1{r^2}\left[\partial_v(r^2\partial_r\psi)+\partial_r\!\left(r^2(\partial_v\psi+D\partial_r\psi)\right)\right].$$

The density identity used here is stated for smooth vector fields, but its coordinate proof uses only first derivatives of their components and the product rule; it therefore holds for $C^1$ vector fields as well. Here $g^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi$ is $C^2$, so the formula is defined and $\Box_g\widetilde\psi$ is $C^1$. In particular the wave equation can be differentiated once in $r$ for a $C^3$ profile. Set $\phi(v,r)=r\psi(v,r)$ and take every $\partial_r$ derivative in this regular ingoing chart. If $[\psi]$ denotes the arbitrary scalar-field unit, then $[\phi]=[\psi]\,\mathrm m$.

Fix $m>0$ and real $q_e,q_m$ with $q_e^2+q_m^2=m^2$, and take the ingoing extremal RN metric and coordinates specified by the spherical test-scalar definition. Let $\psi$ be any admissible neutral spherical $C^3$ solution of $\Box_g\psi=0$, set $\phi=r\psi$, and define its spherical horizon charge by

$$H_\psi(v):=\partial_r\phi(v,m).$$

Then $H_\psi$ is constant for all $v\in\mathbb R$. If this constant is nonzero, the regular ingoing-chart transverse derivative $\partial_r\phi(v,m)$ is nonzero and does not tend to zero along the horizon. If $[\psi]$ is the scalar-field unit, then $[H_\psi]=[\psi]$. This is a local fixed-background statement and asserts no global decay or nonlinear instability.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

Let $I \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be order-convex with at least two elements
([[def-interval]]) and let $f : I \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous on $I$
([[def-continuity-real]]). Call $G : I \to \mathbb{R}$ a **primitive of $f$ on
$I$** when $G$ is differentiable at every point of $I$ as a function on $I$ with
$G' = f$ there ([[def-derivative]]). Then:

1. **Existence.** Fix $c_0 \in I$. The function
   $$F : I \to \mathbb{R}, \qquad F(x) \;:=\; \int_{c_0}^x f$$
   is defined at every $x \in I$ ([[def-oriented-integral]],
   [[def-the-integral-function]]) and is a primitive of $f$ on $I$.
2. **Uniqueness up to a constant.** If $G_1$ and $G_2$ are primitives of $f$ on
   $I$ then there is a real $k$ with $G_1(x) = G_2(x) + k$ for every $x \in I$.
3. **Evaluation.** If $a, b \in I$ with $a < b$ and $G$ is any primitive of $f$
   on $I$, then
   $$\int_a^b f \;=\; G(b) - G(a) .$$

**The scope is exactly the continuous case, and that is not a limitation of the
proof.** An integrable function need not have a primitive, and a function with a
primitive need not be integrable; this corollary is precisely the intersection
where both fundamental theorems apply, and both witnesses are on the companion
page.

Let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}$ with $a < b$ and let $f : [a,b] \to \mathbb{R}$ be
continuous on $[a,b]$ (Continuity of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point of $A$ and on $A$: the $\varepsilon$-$\delta$ condition, its agreement with $\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = f(c)$ at a limit point, and continuity at an isolated point, Intervals of $\mathbb{R}$: the nine order-convex forms, nondegeneracy, and length) and
differentiable at every point of $(a,b)$ as a function on $[a,b]$
(The derivative $f'(c) = \lim_{x \to c} \frac{f(x) - f(c)}{x - c}$ of $f : A \to \mathbb{R}$ at a point $c \in A$ that is a limit point of $A$, and differentiability on a set). Then there is $c \in (a,b)$ with

$$f(b) - f(a) \;=\; f'(c)\,(b - a) .$$

Equivalently, since $b - a \ne 0$, there is $c \in (a,b)$ at which
$f'(c) = \bigl(f(b)-f(a)\bigr)/(b-a)$: the derivative somewhere inside equals
the average rate of change across the whole interval.

**Continuity on the closed interval cannot be dropped.** Differentiability at
every point of $(a,b)$ alone does not suffice: a function on $[0,1]$,
differentiable at every point of $(0,1)$ with derivative constantly $1$, for
which no $c$ works, is exhibited later on this page as a false statement, and
the companion page works the same witness out in full.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

In a local sphere chart with angular metric components $\gamma_{AB}$, the inverse of the ingoing $(v,r)$ metric block is $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&D\end{pmatrix}$ and the full density is $w=r^2\sqrt{\det(\gamma_{AB})}$. For $J^a=g^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi$, spherical symmetry gives $J^v=\psi_r$, $J^r=\psi_v+D\psi_r$, and $J^A=0$. This vector field is $C^2$, so [F3] applies. By [F1], [F4] and metric compatibility, $\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\nabla_aJ^a$. Applying the density formula and cancelling the angular density, which is independent of $v,r$, yields
$$0=\Box_g\widetilde\psi=\frac1{r^2}\left[\partial_v(r^2\psi_r)+\partial_r\!\left(r^2(\psi_v+D\psi_r)\right)\right].$$
Expanding and using equality of the continuous mixed partials gives $2r^2\psi_{vr}+2r\psi_v+\partial_r(r^2D\psi_r)=0$. With $\phi=r\psi$, the identities $2r^2\psi_{vr}+2r\psi_v=2r\phi_{vr}$ and $r^2D\psi_r=D(r\phi_r-\phi)$ reduce this to
$$2\phi_{vr}+D\phi_{rr}+D'\phi_r-\frac{D'}r\phi=0.$$

Let $f(v):=\phi(v,m)$, which is continuous and tends to zero by [A2], and define $F(v):=\int_{v_0}^v f(s)\,ds$ for any fixed $v_0\in\mathbb R$. By [F5], $F$ exists and $F'=f$. Given $\varepsilon>0$, choose $S\ge v_0$ so that $|f(s)|<\varepsilon$ for every $s\ge S$. For each $v>\max\{S,0\}$, the mean value theorem [F6] on $[S,v]$ gives a $c\in(S,v)$ with $F(v)-F(S)=f(c)(v-S)$; hence
$$\left|\frac{F(v)}v\right|\le\frac{|F(S)|}{v}+\varepsilon\frac{v-S}{v}.$$
Taking $v\to+\infty$ gives $\limsup |F(v)/v|\le\varepsilon$. Since $\varepsilon$ was arbitrary, $F(v)/v\to0$.

Differentiate the equation in step 1.1 once in $r$, which is permitted because $\phi$ is $C^3$. The result is
$$2\phi_{vrr}+D\phi_{rrr}+2D'\phi_{rr}+\left(D''-\frac{D'}r\right)\phi_r-\left(\frac{D''}r-\frac{D'}{r^2}\right)\phi=0.$$
Direct differentiation gives $D(m)=D'(m)=0$ and $D''(m)=2/m^2$. Evaluating at $r=m$ and using [F2] therefore yields the exact horizon transport identity
$$\partial_v\phi_{rr}(v,m)=-\frac{H}{m^2}+\frac{\phi(v,m)}{m^3}.$$

Define $P(v):=-H(v-v_0)/m^2+F(v)/m^3$ and $G(v):=\phi_{rr}(v,m)$. By [F5], $F'(v)=\phi(v,m)$, so $P'(v)=-H/m^2+\phi(v,m)/m^3=G'(v)$ by step 2.1. Both $P$ and $G$ are continuous on $[v_0,\infty)$ and differentiable on its interior; [F7] makes $G-P$ constant there. Since $P(v_0)=0$, this gives
$$\phi_{rr}(v,m)-\phi_{rr}(v_0,m)=-\frac{H}{m^2}(v-v_0)+\frac{F(v)}{m^3}.$$
Divide by $v$ and use step 1.2; the fixed terms $\phi_{rr}(v_0,m)/v$ and $Hv_0/(m^2v)$ tend to zero, while $F(v)/(m^3v)\to0$. Therefore $\phi_{rr}(v,m)/v\to-H/m^2$. Since $H\ne0$, the limit is nonzero and its absolute value is $|H|/m^2$, proving the stated linear growth.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), let $(U,x)$ be a
smooth chart, and define the local **metric density** by
$w:=\sqrt{|\det(g_{ab})|}$ on $U$, using the matrix of metric components
in this chart. This definition requires no orientation or volume form. Write
$g^{ab}$ for the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\Gamma^{a}{}_{bc}$ for the Christoffel symbols of $\nabla$ in the chart.

**(a) Derivative of the density.** At every point of $U$,

$$\partial_a w=\tfrac12\,w\,g^{bc}\,\partial_a g_{bc}.$$

**(b) Trace of the Christoffel symbols.** At every point of $U$,

$$\Gamma^{b}{}_{ba}=w^{-1}\partial_a w .$$

**(c) Divergence formula.** For every smooth vector field $J$ on $M$, at every
point of $U$,

$$\nabla_aJ^a=\partial_aJ^a+\Gamma^{a}{}_{ab}J^b=w^{-1}\partial_a\bigl(w\,J^a\bigr),$$

where $\nabla_aJ^a=g^{ab}\nabla_bJ_a$ is the divergence of $J$ contracted with
the metric and $J^a$ are the components of $J$
([[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).

The identity of (c) is a chart formula for a chart-independent scalar: the
right-hand side is independent of the chart, as the left-hand side is.

Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

$$\Box_g\widetilde\psi:=g^{ab}\bigl(\partial_a\partial_b\widetilde\psi-\Gamma^c{}_{ab}\partial_c\widetilde\psi\bigr).$$

The density identity used here is stated for smooth vector fields, but its coordinate proof uses only first derivatives of their components and the product rule; it therefore holds for $C^1$ vector fields as well. Here $g^{ab}\partial_b\widetilde\psi$ is $C^2$, so the formula is defined and $\Box_g\widetilde\psi$ is $C^1$. In particular the wave equation can be differentiated once in $r$ for a $C^3$ profile.
